exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Starting a Business
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lucy: Have you decided what to do after we graduate, Tom?
Tom: Yes. I really want to start my own business. I dream of running a small coffee shop.
Lucy: That's brave. Where will you find the money to begin?
Tom: I've saved some, and I'll ask the bank for a small loan.
Lucy: What do you think will be the biggest challenge?
Tom: Getting the first customers, I suppose. At the start it is always slow.
Lucy: Well, I believe in you. You have always worked hard.
Tom: Thanks, Lucy. If it goes well, maybe one day you can work with me!
exercises.translation_cn: Lucy 问 Tom 毕业后的打算;Tom 想自己创业、开一家小咖啡馆;启动资金来自积蓄和银行小额贷款;他认为最大的挑战是吸引最初的顾客;Lucy 表示支持;Tom 说如果顺利,也许 Lucy 将来能加入他。

exercises.title: U4 听力·独白 A Year-End Reward
exercises.speaker: uk_female
exercises.transcript: Good afternoon, everyone. This has been a wonderful year for our flower company. Because we all worked so hard, our roses are now sold across Asia. To thank you, the company will give every worker a bonus this month. Those who arrived early to pick the flowers before sunrise will receive a little extra. We hope this reward shows how much we value your effort. Next year, with your help, we want to grow even more.
exercises.translation_cn: 下午好,各位。对我们花卉公司来说,这是了不起的一年。因为大家都很努力,我们的玫瑰如今已销往亚洲各地。为感谢大家,公司本月将给每位工人发奖金;那些日出前就来采花的人还会额外多得一点。希望这份奖励能体现我们对你们付出的重视。明年,有了大家的帮助,我们想发展得更好。

questions.stem: Why was it a good year for the company?
options: Everyone worked hard and the roses sold widely.

options: Those who arrived late each day.

exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Opening a Bank Account
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Clerk: Good morning. How can I help you today?
Girl: Hi, I'd like to open my first bank account. I'm starting university next month.
Clerk: Of course. I'd suggest an account with free online banking and no monthly fees.
Girl: That sounds perfect. I want to save a little money each week.
Clerk: Good idea. Even small savings grow over time and earn interest.
Girl: Should I get a credit card too?
Clerk: You can, but use it carefully and always pay your bill on time, or your credit score will fall.
Girl: Thank you. I'll be careful not to go into debt.
exercises.translation_cn: 职员问能帮什么忙;女孩想开第一个银行账户,因为下月要上大学;职员建议办一个免月费、含免费网银的账户;女孩想每周存点钱;职员说小额储蓄会随时间增长并产生利息;关于信用卡,职员提醒要谨慎使用、按时还款,否则信用分会下降;女孩说会小心不让自己负债。

exercises.title: U4 听力·独白 The Joy of Sharing
exercises.speaker: uk_female
exercises.transcript: The sharing economy lets people borrow things instead of buying them. With a phone, you can hire a bike for an hour or rent a room for a night. This saves money for both the lender and the borrower. It also helps the environment, because sharing means fewer cars on the road and less waste. Many people even make new friends while sharing. Of course, users must still protect their personal information. But for most people, sharing is a smart and friendly way to live.
exercises.translation_cn: 共享经济让人们借用而非购买物品。用手机,你可以租一辆自行车骑一小时,或租一个房间住一晚。这为出借者和借用者双方都省钱。它也有利于环境,因为共享意味着路上的车更少、浪费更少。许多人在共享中还结交了新朋友。当然,用户仍须保护个人信息。但对大多数人来说,共享是一种聪明又友好的生活方式。

exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 At the Flower Market
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Buyer: These roses look lovely. How much are they?
Seller: Twenty yuan a bunch. They were picked fresh this morning before sunrise.
Buyer: That's why they smell so sweet. Where are they grown?
Seller: In a valley not far from here, where the roses grow wild.
Buyer: Wonderful. I'll take three bunches for my shop.
Seller: Good choice. If you buy three, I'll give you a small discount.
Buyer: Thank you. Do you sell them online as well?
Seller: Yes, you can order more on our website any time.
exercises.translation_cn: 买家觉得玫瑰很美,问价;卖家说一束二十元,今早日出前刚采的;买家明白了它们为何这么香,问产地;卖家说产自附近一个玫瑰野生生长的山谷;买家要买三束给自己店里;卖家说买三束给个小折扣;买家又问是否网上也卖;卖家说可随时在网站下单。

options: Early in the morning, before sunrise.

exercises.title: U4 听力·独白 Advice for Young Founders
exercises.speaker: uk_female
exercises.transcript: If you dream of starting your own business, here is some advice. First, you need more than a good idea; you also need a clear plan and money to begin. Second, learn from people with more experience, and ask experts for guidance before you start. Third, work hard, but be realistic and know your own limits. Many young people fail because they are too ambitious. Remember, success takes time. With patience and careful planning, your small idea may one day grow into something great.
exercises.translation_cn: 如果你梦想自己创业,这里有几条建议。第一,光有好点子还不够,你还需要清晰的计划和启动资金。第二,向更有经验的人学习,起步前请教专家。第三,努力工作,但要现实,知道自己的极限。许多年轻人失败,是因为太好高骛远。记住,成功需要时间。凭借耐心和周密的计划,你的小点子也许有一天会成长为伟大的事业。

questions.stem: Besides a good idea, what else do you need?
options: A large house and a car.
A clear plan and money to begin.
